description: tools.byAgent for `atlas`: the whole view one agent may call, in one read, and the answer the gate itself would give (TC5 — the same `GrantedSet` union and the same evaluator the step's builder uses, checked row by row against both in the daemon's own suite). All five states are here: `granted_allowed` (the allow that decides, `read`, and the effect class that decides for an MCP tool), `granted_ask` (`webfetch`, an ask that outranks the allow and is NOT a permission — S11), `granted_denied` (bash, refused by a named row), `granted_no_rule` (acme.post, held and unclassified: no rule spoke, which is a different fact from a denial and from "nobody declared it"), and `not_granted` (`todo`, outside the grant set, with no reason because none was sought). MCP names are qualified and appear ONLY for the servers this agent declared against — an agent cannot ask about another agent, and there is no field in which to try (TC9). The list is every tool that EXISTS, not only the granted ones: "may call nothing" and "this tool was never granted to you" are the two answers a grants screen exists to tell apart.

tools.reason: refused: an unclassified tool cannot be called (MC6)
